record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the listed files' contents were not provided.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a refusal-rate outcome after applying a direction-based weight edit, a different intervention from the original activation ablation.
record.gate_note: The README describes per-layer direction evaluation and a basic all-layer variant, but gives no separate outcome for those steps. The listed PROGRESS.md and scripts were not read, so no results are inferred from them.
record.test_reason: The README reports a refusal-rate outcome (50% to ~37%) after difference-in-means direction ablation, done as a weight edit, on LiquidAI LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct. That is a non-Llama hybrid architecture not covered by the original, so this is a new setting. The evidence is a single informal, unreplicated number with no stated prompt set.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The author reports a best refusal rate of ~37% (from 50%) and says some censorship remains. Illegal-activity prompts are only partially uncensored and NSFW is hit or miss. Normal questions are said to work fine.
record.recipe_differences: Abliteration implementation/tool based on the cited HuggingFace blog post. It finds harmful-versus-harmless activation differences at the last token, evaluates directions by layer, and uses weight orthogonalization; the README does not describe projecting out the direction at every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says the recommended version evaluates layers and modifies only those that help; the basic version modifies all layers and can sometimes make things worse. No separate outcome values are given for these variants.
record.problems: The README supplies only one best refusal-rate comparison, without uncertainty, control results, or exact run settings. Its capability statement is qualitative and lacks test details.
record.rows_left_out: No separate results are reported for the basic all-layer variant or layer-selection procedure; the README only characterizes them qualitatively. No results were available from the listed PROGRESS.md or scripts.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal hobby repository (0 stars) with no peer review and no uncertainty. The 50% baseline refusal rate is low, which suggests a mixed or unclear prompt set. The author had to adapt hooks for the LFM2 architecture, which may explain the incomplete removal. Treat this as weak evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Adding the direction; projecting it out at every layer and position; and a broad assessment of other capabilities.
